item.title: NBA HOF Carmelo Anthony adds to Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum drama with personal story
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images NBA HOF Carmelo Anthony adds to Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum drama with personal story appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The fallout between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum has been one of the biggest storylines of the NBA season, and Carmelo Anthony just added some fuel to the fire. Appearing on NBC’s “NBA Showtime” during Tuesday night’s matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers, Anthony recalled being at an event in Cannes with both players shortly before Brown was traded. “When both of those guys, JB and JT, was there kind of right before the trade, it was a weird feeling, right? I don’t know what the feeling was, but it was a weird feeling being in the same environment,” Anthony said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) JUST IN: Carmelo Anthony says that he attended an event with Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown and could feel the tension in the room between them 😳 (via @NBAonNBC , h/t @NBA__Courtside ) pic.twitter.com/ksJHeDiiZk — Polymarket Hoops (@PolymarketHoops) November 11, 2026 “Everybody in that room felt something. And because of that, a lot of conversations and information started, or maybe false information started coming from there.” Still, the 10-time All-Star insisted that there is no bad blood between the two. “Those two guys know what it is, right? There’s no beef. This is two guys who went through what they went through, was successful in Boston, won in Boston,” Anthony added. Things still looked awkward before tipoff on Tuesday, though. In Brown’s first game against his former team since his offseason trade to Philadelphia, Tatum approached him for what looked like a handshake or hug . Brown kept his focus on the ball in his hands, before Tatum tapped him on the chest, gave him a brief side hug and moved on to greet LeBron James. Brown had already made his stance clear before the matchup . “There’s nothing to talk about. He’s on his side, I’m on my side,” he said after the 76ers’ win over the Chicago Bulls. Tatum, on the other hand, has maintained that everything is fine on his end. “I don’t have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him,” he said. On the court, it was Paul George who stole the spotlight in the first half . Sent to Boston in the trade that landed Brown in Philadelphia, George scored 17 points on 7-of-11 shooting as the Celtics took a double-digit lead into the break. Tatum had 13 points, while Brown added eight points, two assists and two steals. Either way, the Tatum-Brown saga does not look like it will be cooling down anytime soon. item.title: 1 improvement Yankees GM Brian Cashman wants to make in 2027 involves media
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-USA TODAY Sports 1 improvement Yankees GM Brian Cashman wants to make in 2027 involves media appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have some decisions to make this offseason regarding where they want to devote their resources to. They have to sort out their infield situation, and they may want to add some depth in the outfield. Acquiring bullpen help is never a bad idea as well for general manager Brian Cashman . Nonetheless, Cashman emphasized that the Yankees organization needs to do a better job of being transparent to the media regarding their players’ injuries after the uncertainty that came with the Aaron Judge situation from last season. “Just externally, how we communicate with you guys, I think we’ll be better at that as we move forward than we were as this 2026 campaign went. I don’t think that’ll be as much of an issue as we move forward,” Cashman said, per Chris Kirschner of The Athletic. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Judge suffered a stress fracture on his first rib on the right side back in May, keeping him out for a lengthy period. He would not return to the Yankees lineup until the eighth of September, which seemed to be right on time to help New York for their postseason push. However, Judge would only play seven more games for the Yankees in 2026 before a right calf strain knocked him out of action and sent him to the injured list . There would then be so many questions regarding whether or not he would be able to return for the postseason, particularly during their ALDS clash against the Tampa Bay Rays, but he would end up missing the rest of the season due to the aforementioned injury. Yankees fans waited with bated breath for Judge’s return, only for the 34-year-old to miss the entire postseason. New York struggled to score runs, as they only put up five runs in their three-game sweep at the Rays’ hands. The hope for the Yankees is that Judge remains mostly healthy next season as they continue their push to end their World Series drought. item.title: Cody Bellinger may be the guy to fill Yankees’ center field void
item.description: Kyle Ross-Imagn Images Cody Bellinger may be the guy to fill Yankees’ center field void appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have been consistently in playoff contention, but they are yet to find their first World Series breakthrough since 2009. In 2026, the Yankees, after winning 93 games in the regular season and advancing to the ALDS after sweeping their rival Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card round, got swept by the eventual AL pennant winner , the Tampa Bay Rays. There are clearly some areas of improvement for the Yankees to focus on. For starters, they will have to address their infield situation this offseason, what with Jazz Chisholm Jr. being a free agent . Perhaps it would be best for the Yankees as well to add some depth to their outfield, as Trent Grisham is also currently a free agent. But for general manager Brian Cashman, he believes that having Cody Bellinger back as a full-time center fielder would be the outcome he’s most comfortable in, as per Gary Phillips of New York Daily News. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bellinger suited up for the Yankees mostly in left field last season, as he played 123 games at that position. But in previous seasons, Bellinger showed that he could be a full-time center fielder. The Yankees simply relied on rookie Spencer Jones to play his comfort position of center field last season, and Grisham, the team’s other outfield option, also played the vast majority of his games at that position. Nonetheless, Cashman believes that Jones is more of a natural left fielder, so perhaps having Bellinger back at center helps improve the team’s outfield defense. Bellinger was solid for the Yankees last season. He missed time due to a hamstring strain, but he still played in 132 games last season and finished with 17 home runs and 73 runs batted in. He had an OPS of .767, and his outfield defense rated above average, helping him finish the campaign with a 3.5 fWAR. The 31-year-old signed a five-year, $162.5 million contract with the Yankees last offseason. He has an opt-out prior to the 2028 season, which, if he exercises, would have him leave three years and $77.5 million on the table. item.title: Stacy’s Streamers: Five Players to Start in Week 10
item.description: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, bringing new faces to new places and a few moves that could shake up fantasy lineups. We’ll get into some of those below. Meanwhile, we’re pouring one out for fantasy managers missing their stars like Puka Nacua and Michael Wilson, who landed on injured reserve this week. Whether you’re replacing an injured starter, navigating the bye-week blues or just looking for a little upside, I’ve got five players worth considering for Week 10. Bye Weeks: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay QB: Drew Lock, Seattle vs. Las Vegas Why I like him: Sam Darnold has already been ruled out for Week 10, so Lock will be under center for the Seahawks. The Raiders have been particularly vulnerable to opposing quarterbacks this season, allowing an average passer rating of 103.6, more than two passing touchdowns and 248.7 passing yards per game. Lock has also developed a strong connection with star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, posting an elite passer rating when targeting JSN, who commands more than 40% of Lock’s targets this season. And obviously, I don’t need to tell you to start JSN. The Play: Lock is a legitimate starting option in Week 10, especially with one of the NFL’s most dangerous receivers at his disposal. RB: Audric Estimé, New Orleans vs. Carolina Why I like him: It’s his third NFL season, and Estimé is officially entering his main-character era. In his first start with the Saints, Estimé wasted no time making an impression, turning 15 carries into 72 rushing yards and a touchdown. Now, in Week 10, he gets a dream matchup against the Panthers, who have allowed the second-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season. The only team worse? The Saints themselves. Cue Alanis Morissette, because isn’t it ironic? Carolina is also surrendering an average of 1.4 touchdowns per game to the position, tied for the league high. With a favorable matchup and an opportunity to establish himself in the Saints’ backfield, Estimé has plenty working in his favor. The Play: Estimé offers legitimate RB2 upside this week, particularly with an excellent opportunity to find the end zone for the second consecutive week. WR: Xavier Hutchinson, Houston vs. Cleveland Why I like him: In a surprising turn of events, the Texans’ offense has been doing its part to keep Houston competitive this season. C.J. Stroud and company are averaging 26.1 points per game and rank eighth in passing yards per play. Perhaps even more surprising? Xavier Hutchinson is leading Houston’s wide receivers in slot alignment, lining up there on 52.8% of his snaps. Yes, that’s even more than Tank Dell. That could work in his favor this week against a Cleveland defense that allows slot receivers 12.9 fantasy points per game and 8.96 yards per target. Hutchinson has also scored in two of his last three games, giving fantasy managers another reason to take notice. The Play: Hutchinson could deliver a sneaky flex-worthy performance for fantasy managers

item.title: Miami With Best Path To College Football Playoff Title Game
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If the CFP started today, Miami’s road back to the finals would seem like a cakewalk for the Hurricanes. Assuming Malachi Toney returns, Miami has an incredible opportunity to run the table to the College Football Playoff finals. Related: Iowa Deserves Position In Latest College Football Playoff Ranking The committee revealed what the 12-team bracket would look like today if the season ended. Assuming the Hurricanes get Toney back for the postseason, things would shape up very, very nicely for the former No. 1 team in the country. The Million Dollar Question Revolves Around Malachi Toney While they put up points against Notre Dame, there was definitely a piece missing for Miami last weekend. That was to be expected after losing a Heisman Trophy contender earlier in the week. Related: Can Miami Overcome The Loss Of Star Wide Receiver Malachi Toney? Toney not only stretched opposing defenses, but he also helped open things up for everyone else in the passing game. Miami will have more time to work on overcoming the sudden loss. But there is no replacing Toney with one player. Darian Mensah is going to be counted on to look more and more like a Heisman frontrunner. Mark Fletcher and Javian Mallory will be counted on more and more. And the receiving crew will need to make plays. What Remains On The Schedule For The Hurricanes? Miami should be able to handle things from here on out. They welcome Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College for home games, looking at an 11-1 record heading to the ACC title game. Wake Forest would be the opponent right now for the Hurricanes in the conference championship. Louisville and SMU sit just outside the top of the standings. If things play out accordingly, that would be 12-1 with the lone loss coming to Notre Dame on the road. And the Irish are almost a lock to make the CFP. Looking At Miami’s Projected College Football Playoff Road The committee released the 12-team bracket on Tuesday night. Georgia, Utah, Alabama and UCLA all received byes as the Top-4 teams in the rankings. Here's what the #CFP bracket would like if the season ended today 👀🏆 pic.twitter.com/5Gekzx3WdU — CFP (@CFBPlayoff) November 11, 2026 Miami is currently seventh, pairing them up with BYU in the first round. While a strong team, the Cougars would have trouble hanging with the Hurricanes. From there, they get BYU’s rival, Utah, in the quarterfinals. The game being on a neutral field would definitely play into this one, taking out the rabid fan base of the Utes. Again, player for player, it would be hard bet against Miami in this one. That leaves either Alabama, Texas or Kentucky. Alabama and Texas are the two more likely teams, with the Longhorns maybe getting a tick above the Crimson Tide. Texas can match the Hurricanes in terms of talent, leaving it up to the stars to decide this one. Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Paul George revenge game fuels Boston Celtics blowout of Philadelphia 76ers
item.description: In a game that many saw as a clash of the Eastern Conference titans currently at the top of the standings to start the 2026-27 NBA regular season, the reality was a 123-101 road blowout win for the Boston Celtics over the Philadelphia 76ers . The Celtics were in control for nearly the entire game, trailing by 1 point briefly before Boston blew it open in the final frame with a barrage of makes from beyond the arc. That the Celtics held the Sixers to just 30 percent from deep on a night they shot 45 percent from 3 helped quite a bit, as did winning the shot attempt battle 95-79. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Hawks fall short in OT to Virginia Tech, 93-88
item.description: SIOUX CITY, IOWA - NOVEMBER 10: Cooper Koch #8 of the Iowa Hawkeyes drives against Amani Hansberry #13 of the Virginia Tech Hokies during the second half at Tyson Events Center on November 10, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Iowa Hawkeyes (2-1) got slow starts in each of the three frames tonight in a 93-88 loss to Virginia Tech (3-0). The most notable was not scoring a field goal until 0:44 left in the overtime frame. Despite having a chance to tie at the end, Cooper Koch couldn’t make his 3 point attempt amidst a career night. Giving up 93 points is never Ben McCollum’s preferred style and they struggled to contain the Hokie guards, Ben Hammond & Jaylen Curry, who combined for 57 points on 18/34 shooting and 16/18 from the line. Curry’s 3 pointer in overtime proved to be enough distance for Tech as the Hawks couldn’t get it inside of 2 after that. It was a game riddled with fouls and the Hawks finished 66% (31/47) from the line. The biggest of which was Ty’reek Coleman missing on his final attempt with less than 2 seconds left in regulation. Andrew McKeever couldn’t convert the putback quick enough, which allowed VT to come away with the victory in Sioux City’s Tyson Center. The flipside of foul trouble was Kael Combs who lived in foul trouble for the bulk of the game with 2 early ones before the first television timeout, a third later in the first half, and a fourth right out of the break. Thankfully Coleman performed well off the bench with 20 points on 7/10 shooting. Career night for Cooper Koch Despite missing his final attempt of the game, Koch was aggressive all night, with 15/17 from the line en route to a career high 26 points. He was just 5/11 from the field and 1/5 from 3 but he played incredibly hard for all 45 minutes of the game. Many of his free throw attempts came on drives and post ups where he pulled out the Kevin Durant rip throw. Iowa will need to see him take more shots. Koch was joined in double digits by Coleman, Isaia Howard (13 on 3/5 from deep), and Combs (10 points on 4/4). Offensive rebounding kept the Hawks in it Iowa rebounded 18 of 35 opportunities, good for 18 second chance points. It came from unexpected sources – McKeever got his 3 but Coleman and Howard added 3 of their own. While Iowa went after size in the portal, much of the rebounding gains tonight happened from Iowa’s guards. High leverage free throw shooting hurts Iowa Coleman missed the second of 2 attempts down the stretch and then he & Koch combined for 3/5 in the extra frame. Any one of those misses very easily could have flipped it for Iowa. Overall the 31/47 is going to add some frustration to the loss but 7 of Iowa’s 16 misses came from Cam Manyawu & McKeever who went just 2/9. They’re not good FT shooters but they have to be better than that. Next up: Sunday, November 15th at 2:00p vs Creighton in Des Moines, IA

item.title: Louisville Defeats Lindenwood 71-35
item.description: Lindenwood came into the Yum and played hard for 4 quarters but the biggest suspense of the night was whether their coach, Phil Sayers, was going to put freshman Brynn Owens into the game. She had a large contingent of determined and loud fans from up the road in Indiana who got even the Louisville fans to chant for her to be played. Finally in the last few minutes of the game he gave the people what they wanted and there was much rejoicing. Tajianna Roberts led both teams in scoring with 15. Amiya Joyner had a double-double with 11 points and 10 rebounds. Mackenly Randolph should be cleared for the game on Thursday but Elif Istanbulluoglu returned to play after an ankle injury and had 5 rebounds and 2 points. Virginia Tech transfer Carys Baker came out of her shooting slump to finally get her 1000th point. She finished the game with 12 points and 5 rebounds. After the game Carys said, “For me obviously the last couple of games were hard just going scoreless but I think with my teammates they have so much confidence in me for me to be able to knock those down. Staying in the gym and staying positive I always want to be a team player so I didn’t let it affect me. Everyone was telling me to go out there and have fun, and I think that’s what I did.” Coach Walz said, “I thought our effort, especially on the defensive end, in the first half was extremely good. We played hard. We played focused. The second half we got a little carried away trying to steal it every time instead of having good fundamentals and trying to keep someone in front of us. We’ve got to get a lot better real quick at guarding the ball. We’re allowing way too many straight line drives and it’s going to be a problem.” He added, “I’m hoping we can improve without having to get our butts kicked and all of a sudden it’s an eye opener like oh sh*t he actually knows what he’s talking about.” Next up the Cards hit the road to play Ball State on Thursday. item.title: CFP rankings Week 11 winners and losers: Indiana falls below 2-loss SEC crowd, ACC jilted
item.description: CFP rankings Week 11 winners and losers: Indiana falls below 2-loss SEC crowd, ACC jilted originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The College Football Playoff committee is just giving Curt Cignetti more material for his radio show. item.title: UCLA football makes stunning move in CFP rankings after initial snub
item.description: Given another week to assess UCLA, the College Football Playoff selection committee had a different take on the Bruins. Move them up. Way up. In the wake of an impressive road victory over Minnesota, UCLA rose to No. 4 in the CFP rankings released Tuesday night. That’s four spots above where the Bruins were slotted only a week ago . Most importantly, moving into the top four puts UCLA (9-0 overall, 6-0 Big Ten) on track to receive a first-round bye into the quarterfinal round of the 12-team playoff. UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against Minnesota in an NCAA college football game Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, in Minneapolis. AP Photo/Abbie Parr So, did the CFP selection committee make a mistake last week when it came to the Bruins? “I don’t think it was an admission of them being ranked too low,” Hunter Yurachek, chairman of the CFP selection committee, said on a conference call with reporters. “I think what we’re seeing with the parity around college football [is] that we now have only two remaining unbeaten teams and UCLA is one of those, and I think they continue to improve as a team. “The defense has been steady and really dominant all season, they’ve had an established running game and their quarterback play is getting better — their backup quarterback that has been filling in really seemed to find his way, especially in the fourth quarter of that game against Minnesota.” Notre Dame wide receiver Micah Gilbert (14) scores a touchdown during the second half of an NCAA college football game against Miami, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. AP Photo/Paul Barnick Yurachek was alluding to quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who replaced the injured Nico Iamaleava a month ago, throwing 75-yard touchdown passes on back-to-back offensive plays to help the Bruins pull away for a 34-20 victory over the Golden Gophers. This is UCLA’s highest spot ever in the CFP rankings after its No. 8 ranking last week tied its previous high from the 2014 season. The only teams ranked ahead of the Bruins were No. 1 Georgia, No. 2 Utah and No. 3 Alabama. UCLA and Utah are the last remaining unbeaten teams in major college football. The Bruins’ move was part of a major shakeup in which no team remained in the same CFP spot as a week ago. USC (7-2, 4-2) rose two spots to No. 18 and has a chance to vastly improve its standing Saturday when it faces No. 9 Indiana, which dropped five spots despite not playing last weekend. Should the Bruins secure a first-round bye, they’ll need to come up with a plan to avoid the fate of nearly every predecessor in that spot — teams with byes have gone only 1-7 in the quarterfinals since the playoff expanded to 12 teams for the 2024 season.
